items.note: Association, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891 all in Story 1.
Gives payment by butterfat test not weight, but never states the second bolded clause, that the test of the station where he delivers governs.
Story 1: Article VII was 'the mechanism that made everything that followed matter financially'.
List item scored on its core fact: Teague bookkeeper and Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green are in Section A. Loomis is named but not as secretary.
Section A calls Selby Vose manager but gives neither son-of-Gideon nor 1913. Those appear only in B3, and D3 gives the wrong year, 1911 (deducted separately).
Thin: Story 8 names the ledger's 'station gain' entry (the bolded element). It gives no 1898 origin and no 5.25%. Shared-element rule: the bare ledger line is credited here only.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, opened 4 May 1896, glass 'borrowed of Larrow Green'.
Core mechanism given in Stories 5 and 7: weighed at intake, short pipette charge into a bottle graduated for a full charge. Composite sample not mentioned. List item, core fact.
Ammon & Sons Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; 1898 rejected.
Six dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Story 7: a proportionally low reading 'every time, regardless of season, explaining both the size and the constancy of the gap'; Story 2 gives 0.19.
Section A never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
1861, twenty-nine seasons from 1896, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Thin: Story 8 has the station test book kept by Keddie from 1896 (bolded element). Its contents and the correction routine are not described.
Summary leaf missing: the 1896 average of 3.80 appears nowhere; only the 3.61 long-run figure is given.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is not given; credited on the core fact.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.
1919 circular present, but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why (both bolded).
Died February 1934 under the imputation; test book impounded 1925, Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Says the scales agreed, but leaves the start date open among 1897, 1898 and 1900. The bolded 'from 1 January 1897' is never settled.
Story 2 gives the Hollow-vs-Green comparison (3.61 vs 3.78) as 'a gap of about 0.19 points', conflating the visible 0.17 gap with the true 0.19 shortfall. The key says this loses the item.
Says the Grigg committee 'sampled the six Hessel Bottom herds through 1908'. That is the whole-of-1908 corruption; the correct period is Jan-Mar 1908.
200,000 lb at 3.42 given, but Section A never says the loss was proportional so richer herds lost more (no Vose Jerseys comparison). C2 even applies a flat 0.19.
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962.
Factory, Redlow Ridge and Vessey County given. The founder Jerome Cudd is not named in Section A; the key says Cudd gates the point.
Four of six farms, summer milk over Redlow Ridge, 1915-1930.
Own bench and own glass, the factory's own records, Vessey County, described as independent corroboration. At least two elements.
Same milk recorded 3.78-3.82 at Alder Corners for sixteen seasons, against the station's 3.61.
States the comparison refutes both the watering and wet-hay theories for that milk.
Rosalie Cudd copied the figures for Ivy in 1958 (core fact). 'Daughter' appears only in E14.
Section A has Strawn retiring in 1936 but no 1907 start. D2 and F give 1908 (deducted separately).
Strawn's lactometer checks are not in Section A; only D2 and F mention them.
Section A says only 'condemned in 1923'. No 12 June date and no burette; those are in C5 and F.
Never says Strawn recorded no figure for the deficiency.
Replacement glass, the 1924 average of 3.80 and the unconnected rise are not in Section A.
Crate to the station loft; notebooks to the state office in 1936 and the college library in 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Frick; 17 March, then two sittings in the station weigh room; award four days after 30 April.
Watering (manager's side), theft (Teague), wet hay (1908 report); no cause established.
Lists the four books including the inspector's notebook, but not the second bolded element: that the notebook held the answer and was read for its other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no cause found; $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station's own account.
Section A has neither the one-fifth-of-$19,000 point nor the award being charged to the account where the 'gain' had accumulated.
Granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, with Vaught.
Story 8: the records were 'never in the same room' until Ivy assembled them.
February 1958, station loft, nine; eleven rejected.
9 March 1958, 16.72 vs 17.6, about 95%. The 0.88 c.c. figure is only in C4b; credited on the core fact.
Section A never says every test read 95% of true, 3.61 where 3.80 stood; the true 3.80 is absent from A.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 and the ledger identity are all absent from Section A (A mentions only r11's 118,000).
Bulletin 471, October 1958, clears him; 24 years after his death and 33 after 1925 stated.
Granddaughter.
Duncan's daughter, Duncan Ansel's son (r18, r22).
Second cousins, derived through Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Full vs half sibling left open by the sources; does not change the degree.
Son of Gideon Vose.
Defending his father's Article VII payment-by-test rule.
Asserts 'No genuine relationship existed... the sources resolve in favor of no relationship'.
Treats a family member's denial as settling the question; says no document is silent either way.
0.95; one part in twenty.
Applies a flat 0.19: true test 3.61, 7,220 lb, owed 380 lb. Key: 3.60, 7,200, 360.
5.00% of true and 5.26% of credited, both denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
Gives 'just over 26 years', not the exact 26 years and 6 weeks the exact-match tolerance requires (25 full years and the reason are given).
Abstention A02: verdict 'cannot be determined', lean toward Sill explicitly declined.
Variable: the measuring glass (own vs borrowed).
Herds, pasture/season, tester, scales.
Says only that tests 'rose markedly' and fell back; no 3.80 or 3.61.
Cause traveled with the glass, not farms, feed or tester; limit stated (mechanism and size unidentified, borrowed glass accuracy unknown).
Brant weigh book (r09), Strawn lactometer (r06), Alder Corners book (r10): three valid reasons from three narrators.
Independence argued; Alder Corners and Strawn named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention A09 asserted: 'no, Wilbur Teague... apparently never questioned the ledger entries'.
Yes, he knew the station tested low; cites the 1919 circular.
Only two of five correct (signed the ledger sheets, 1919 circular). Gives manager from 1911 instead of 1913; no hearing argument or glassware-silence point in B-G.
Abstention A03 asserted: the station-gain line is 'documentary proof' he reviewed the credited-vs-received discrepancy every year.
1924 average 3.90/3.85 resolved to 3.80 by arithmetic and log; hearing year 1924/1926 resolved to 1925; crate 1899 rejected against the invoice. Capped at 3.
Pairs named with breakers: $3,500 (r01, r21), five dozen (r11, r21), six weeks (r05, r16), 44M (r05, r12), eleven pipettes (r12, r19), and others. Capped at 3.
A10 (Article VII year) declined, citing the lost minute book. A04 and A06 not treated as abstention conflicts.
r18 1868 vs 82 in 1948; r11 16.27 cascade vs one part in twenty; r03 Ashlin vs Larrow Green.
Cause and 16.72/17.6 given, but it never derives 0.19 as 5% of 3.80 and treats 0.19 as a flat constant (explicitly so in C2). No 1896 onset evidence.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings (the '1908' start is deducted separately).
Theft (Teague) defeated by the 1911 interval with the same tester, among others.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, against a flat year-round gap.
Abstention A07 asserted: 'The 1925 board of arbitration never examined the condemned glassware'.

Abstention A05 asserted: the evidence 'indicates he suspected the glass specifically from 1911 onward' (and Story 4: 'Ansel suspected his own equipment as early as 1911'). The later hedge does not undo the verdict sentence.
Summary is about 159 words; the limit is 150.
Only four record series named (weigh book, ledger, inspector's log, bulletin). No test book, invoice, Alder Corners book, minutes or arbitration record.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure.
About 5% short, 1897, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named: both ends covered.

Corruption: Strawn's circuit begun 1908 ('from 1908 forward' D2, 'from 1908 on' F)
Corruption: circular sent to eleven families, resolved as fact in E15 (F058)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved 'no relationship' (B4)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'never questioned the ledger entries' (D2)
Gullibility A03: manager knew of the understatement via the station-gain line (D3)
Gullibility A07: board 'never examined the condemned glassware' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester believed it was the glass (F; Story 4)
